title: Module 15 Capstone: Choose the Test
intro: This is the skill the whole course builds. Each item describes a study. Pick the analysis that fits the design and the data.

items.q: Compare the mean anxiety of 40 students with the published population mean. The population SD is unknown.
items.why: One sample mean against a known population mean with unknown sigma calls for the one-sample t.

items.q: Compare the mean score of students randomly assigned to online or in-person teaching.
items.why: Two separate groups with a numeric outcome.

items.q: Measure the same 25 patients before and after therapy and compare mean symptom scores.
items.why: The same people are measured twice.

items.q: Compare mean test scores across three teaching methods.
items.why: Three or more independent groups call for ANOVA.

items.q: Examine whether hours of exercise are linearly related to mood scores.
items.why: Two numeric variables and a question about association.

items.q: Use study hours and high school GPA to predict college GPA.
Test whether choice of major (psychology, biology, business) is related to preferring online or in-person classes.
Test whether students pick each of four study locations equally often.
items.why: One categorical variable compared with an expected distribution.

items.q: Compare mean recall for two study methods crossed with two test delays.
items.why: Two factors and a possible interaction.

items.q: Relate a dichotomous variable (smoker or not) to a numeric score.
o: Point-biserial correlation, or an independent t test
items.why: A two-category variable with a numeric outcome is handled by either approach.
